items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: I was taking a few lessons from Paul Barbrand, as I said before.

ctx.x: What about your relatives that either sang or played music? You mentioned that before. What, that, my daddy? Yeah, your daddy.

Well, my daddy was, he used to sing in a quartet. Mm-hmm. You know, the old barbershop quartets? Mm-hmm. Back in the early hundreds. 1900s, so he was a bass songster. And he was considered one of the best that they had in the third ward. Yeah, I got it. Well, my first instrument was piano. My mother was trying to get me to learn piano. And I had a cousin that was a wonderful pianist. And he tried to learn it, but my interest was mostly in drums. Because I used to take the rungs of the chair and go around beating…
Did you, do you remember your cousin's name?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: Then I met Paul Barbrand. Well, he was gonna learn me how to read music... he used to come by the house I was living down on... and give me a few lessons, learn me how to read the notes.

ctx.x: Okay, well we're interviewing Joe Watkins this March 24th, 1969. Just going from what you're about to say, Joe, about when you started music.

When I started, I started in 1920s. Well that was quite a few years after George Lewis and Paul Barbrain. Well I always did love drums because I was born in the third ward and that was, a section for jazz probably because Lee Armstrong was from that ward. He was born and raised around there. And I don't know about Joe Oliver because I always heard that Joe was not exactly from the Orlins. But it was him, Lee Armstrong, Funk Johnson, and you had Manuel Moneta. And, uh, was this other fella's name, uh, was a good…
What sort of date was this? Huh? What date was this about?
